expectations.text: Identifies what files to read (SPEC.md, PROMPT.md, meta.json, recon files)
expectations.evidence: Step 1 lists all files: SPEC.md, PROMPT.md, meta.json, recon/architecture.md, relevant_code.md, conventions.md, plus lite-mode plan artifacts (draft_plan_1.md, validation.md).

expectations.text: Evaluates completeness (architecture, data model, API contracts, edge cases, testing)
expectations.evidence: Covers core link generation, database schema, API endpoints, frontend integration, access control, link expiration, and testing. Less structured than with-skill but touches all areas.

expectations.text: Evaluates feasibility (technical risks, scope proportionality, dependencies)
expectations.evidence: Addresses token entropy, rate limiting/brute-force, information leakage, scope creep checks (analytics, OG tags, collaborative viewing), and data exposure risks.

expectations.text: Evaluates alignment with original issue (Job Story match, Promise fulfillment, constraint respect)
expectations.evidence: Step 3 describes cross-referencing: 'Requirement coverage — Does every acceptance criterion from issue #42 have a corresponding implementation plan in the spec?' Also checks scope creep and architecture fit.

expectations.text: Provides a structured review with clear verdict (ready/needs work)
expectations.evidence: Clear verdict: 'Not yet ready to approve' with specific rationale about security surface area and lite mode's lack of red team review.

expectations.text: Lists specific action items if gaps are found
expectations.evidence: Three specific concerns (security coverage, access control boundaries, expiration lifecycle) plus 4 recommended next steps including re-running in full mode.

expectations.text: Does NOT proceed to implementation (user explicitly said don't implement)
expectations.evidence: Does not mention implementation or handoff at all. Stops at review verdict and recommended next steps.
